whenToUse: People leave and discard unsaved changes.
Right before something irreversible, such as deleting or resetting.
A mistake would be costly, as with paying or sending.
whenNotToUse: The action can be undone (a toast with undo interrupts less).
You'd ask so often that people press confirm out of habit.
The system raises an urgent situation first (use an alert dialog).

alternatives.name: Modal Dialog
alternatives.reason: A window that needs input or explanation beyond confirming.

alternatives.name: Alert Dialog
alternatives.reason: A warning raised by the system, not by people.

accessibility: Open it with the native <dialog> showModal() to trap focus and make the background inert.
Put the cancel button first with initial focus, so pressing Enter out of habit doesn't run the action.
Esc and a click on the backdrop count as cancel (false).
Name the buttons for what will actually happen, such as Leave, instead of OK.
